scenario: Coach at the range on a phone shows a student why their driver slices: path -4, face 0. The face points at the target and the path swings across it.
focus: Shot name (a slice or fade family), where it finishes, the start line (on the target line) and the curve to the right. The path -4 and face 0 numbers.

scenario: A lefty student hooks their 7-iron. The coach opens the swing controls on a phone to show that the face is closed to the path, and that the ball starts left and turns hard right for a left-hander.
focus: Shot name (a hook), that the hand is set to Left, the curve direction for a left-hander, and the path and face sliders with their values and words.

scenario: Coach shows one of the nine windows on a phone: the high draw with a 7-iron for a PGA Tour player.
focus: The selected window (High draw), the shot name and finish, and the recipe numbers (path, face, attack, loft) for that window.

scenario: Coach pins the student's slice (path -4, face 0) as A, then dials in path +3 and face +1 to show the fix as B, on a phone.
focus: Two tracers on the range (A and B) that can be told apart, the shot names for A and B, and the A/B/difference table for carry, curve and start line.

scenario: Coach shows an LPGA player's pitching wedge fade on a phone: path -3, face -1. The same face-to-path as a driver, but a short club, so much less curve.
focus: The shot name, finish, and how little the ball curves in yards. The face to path number.

scenario: A student opens the lab on a phone for the first time with the default 7-iron and PGA Tour player, before touching anything.
focus: A first-time screen: is the shot name obvious, is the ball flight visible, is it clear what to touch next.

scenario: Coach on a phone shows how hitting up on the driver (attack +4) raises launch and lowers spin. The Side view tab shows the launch angle.
focus: Launch angle and spin rate numbers, the Side profile view, the attack angle value.

scenario: Coach holds a phone sideways and shows a PGA Tour driver draw: path +3, face +1. The ball starts right of target and curves back left.
focus: Shot name, finish, the range and tracer (short screen), key numbers, and whether the controls are visible beside the range.

scenario: Coach shows the difference between a push and a pull on a phone in landscape. This is a push: path +3 and face +3 with a 6-iron. The face sets the start line, and face equals path so the ball does not curve.
focus: Shot name (push), starts right and no curve, path and face sliders and values, all readable on a 390 px tall screen.

scenario: Coach taps Fly all nine on a phone in landscape to show the whole nine-window chart with every tracer on the range.
focus: Nine tracers visible on the range with their numbers, and the window grid. Whether the range is still legible with nine tracers.

scenario: Coach pins an amateur 7-iron with path -3 and face 0, then closes the face to -3 in landscape on a phone to show the face controls the start line.
focus: Pinned A and live B tracers, the change in start line, the compare table.

scenario: Coach on an iPad in landscape teaches that the face sets the start line: path 0, face +3 with a 7-iron. The ball starts right of the target.
focus: Start line (3 degrees right), shot name, the face slider, launch direction number.

scenario: Coach picks the low fade window on an iPad in landscape to show a lower flight with a left-to-right curve.
focus: Selected window, its recipe numbers, the shot label, the range and tracer.

scenario: Coach mirrors an iPad to a small screen and taps Present for an amateur 5-wood slice.
focus: Presentation layout: big shot name, the range, key tiles, and the slim control bar.

scenario: A student's slice to a draw on an iPad held upright: pin the slice (driver, path -4, face 0), then set path +3 and face +1.
focus: Both tracers and their labels, the compare table with the difference column, and the shot names for A and B.

scenario: A lefty student's 7-iron draw on an iPad held upright. A left-hander's draw starts left of the target and curves back right, the mirror of a right-hander's draw, and the lab must show it that way.
focus: Shot name (draw), the hand set to Left, and the curve direction on the range and top view consistent with a left-handed draw.

scenario: Coach on an iPad shows what hitting down on the driver (attack -5) does to launch and spin for an amateur.
focus: Launch angle, spin rate and attack angle numbers, and the attack slider (open in the drawer).

scenario: Coach in the studio opens the lab on a laptop with the default PGA Tour 7-iron, a straight shot, as the starting point for a lesson.
focus: Shot name (Straight), where it finishes, the range and tracer, the key numbers.

scenario: Coach shows an LPGA driver fade on a laptop: path -2, face -1. The ball starts left of target and drifts right.
focus: Shot name, the start line to the left and the drift right, the path, face and face-to-path values.

scenario: Coach runs Fly all nine on a laptop to show all nine windows of the 7-iron for a PGA Tour player.
focus: Nine tracers on the range, the nine-window grid, and whether each window can be matched to its tracer.

scenario: A student's slice to a draw on a laptop with Compare: A is path -4, face 0 with a driver, B is path +3, face +1.
focus: A and B tracers, the compare table, the change in curve and start line, shot names.

scenario: Coach in the studio on a laptop shows a 7-iron hook: path +6, face +1. The face is 5 degrees closed to the path, so the ball starts slightly right and hooks left. The coach wants the first screen to show what caused it.
focus: Shot name (a hook), start line and curve, path, face and face-to-path values, and whether any view of face and path at impact is on the first screen.

scenario: Coach shows a PGA Tour 3-wood push on a laptop: path +3, face +3.
focus: Shot name (push), starts right with no curve, the controls next to the range.

scenario: Coach in the studio on a laptop wants the student to see why an amateur driver with path -4 and face 0 loses distance: the coach reads launch angle and spin rate against their ideal bands.
focus: Launch angle and spin rate (and face to path) readable on the first screen without scrolling, with a clear in-band or out-of-band signal on each.

scenario: Coach on a studio TV runs Present for a PGA Tour driver draw: path +3, face +1. Students sit across the room.
focus: From across a room: the shot name and finish, the tracer, the key tiles. Size, contrast and whether the control bar stays out of the way.

scenario: Coach on a TV shows an amateur driver slice in Present mode: path -4, face 0.
focus: Shot name, the curve direction on the range, key tiles, readable from across the room.

scenario: Coach runs Fly all nine and then goes to Present on a TV so the students see the whole nine-window pattern.
focus: Nine tracers on a big range, whether each can be told apart, and the shot label state after the sequence.

scenario: Coach pins a slice as A and moves to the draw as B, then presents on a TV to show both tracers together.
focus: A and B tracers with their tags, the shot name, and whether the difference between A and B can be read without the compare table.

scenario: Coach in the studio shows a wedge shot (LPGA pitching wedge, path -3, face -1) on a 1080p TV without Present mode.
focus: How the page uses a wide screen: the range size, the tiles, the controls, empty space, hierarchy.

scenario: A 4K TV in the studio in Present mode with a PGA Tour driver hook: path +5, face +1.
focus: Text and control sizing at 3840x2160, the shot name, whether the layout scales without empty areas or tiny text.
